subject.title: RFC: Period-based popularity for publishers, skills, and plugins

question: Should ClawHub implement a shared Weekly/Monthly/All time popularity contract across publishers/creators, skills, and plugins before adding browse-page period tabs, and what V1 scoring and attribution rules should it use?
rationale: Current main has partial seven-day skill/plugin trending but no publisher temporal rollup or monthly/snapshot-pinned contract, so implementation would encode product and data semantics that maintainers have not settled.

options.title: Foundation-first shared contract
options.body: Define V1 scoring, event-time ownership attribution, low-activity behavior, package backfill or warm-up policy, and snapshot retention before shipping the UI tabs.

options.title: Expose only existing trending surfaces
options.body: Limit UI to the current seven-day skill/plugin Trending behavior and avoid publisher period popularity until publisher rollups exist.

options.title: Defer the discovery change
options.body: Keep all browse pages on existing all-time/recommended/trending controls until marketplace discovery ranking becomes a higher roadmap priority.

recommendation.title: Foundation-first shared contract
recommendation.body: Define V1 scoring, event-time ownership attribution, low-activity behavior, package backfill or warm-up policy, and snapshot retention before shipping the UI tabs.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the RFC and have prior merged history on the publishers/creators browse surface that anchors the visible UI request.
